summary: Cleanly replay Issue #61 on current main: the chunked restore validator now accepts and strictly verifies the exact managed-context metadata schema emitted by the same kernel (`kind=file`, canonical absolute `path`, exact UTF-8 `bytes`) instead of requiring nonexistent `read_bytes`/`canonical_path` fields.

pointers: Issue#61: chunked recovery restores managed context metadata emitted by the same kernel

steps: Rebuilt the repair from current main after Issue #64 merged rather than carrying the stale #98 branch forward.

Moved the multilingual managed-context recovery regression into a dedicated test file and made Windows temp-tree cleanup retry only after awaiting runtime.dispose(), so filesystem-handle settlement cannot masquerade as a product failure.

Applied the production change through a line-guarded one-shot workflow: it required exactly one legacy read_bytes line and its exact canonical_path continuation, derived indentation from the live file, replaced only those two expressions with the writer-owned strict schema checks, ran git diff --check, committed, pushed, and self-deleted.

evidence.note: Memory and Ubuntu full gate were green; Windows typecheck/build and the product recovery assertion succeeded but the test failed only during immediate rmSync cleanup with EPERM.
The unique live-code guard matched, production patch committed as ff31da1, and the one-shot workflow removed itself.
Final dual-OS clean-replay gate will run after this record and PR are created.

limitations: This fix intentionally does not change checkpoint chunk wire encoding; UTF-8/base64 transport is tracked by #82.
Sequence/completeness/aggregate validation of checkpoint_chunk remains tracked by #81.
